_readme: Lisa's OWN reviewed snapshot of what this repository's merge rules require, and of what each `skip_jobs` token would silence. `scripts/check-skipped-required-checks.mjs` (here: `typescript/copy-overwrite/scripts/…`) makes the two police each other.

This file did not exist until #2933. Without it the `🔒 Skipped Required Checks` job printed `skipping` and reported SUCCESS on every pull request since it shipped — the guard against silencing required checks was itself silently green, on the repository that owns the epic against exactly that.

`required_contexts` was transcribed live on `baseline_fetched_at` from the two branch rulesets named in `ruleset.ids`, byte for byte, emoji and the ' / ' separator included. Reproduce it with: gh api repos/CodySwannGT/lisa/rulesets/ID --jq '.rules[] | select(.type=="required_status_checks") | .parameters.required_status_checks[].context'
Both rulesets carry the same ref condition (~DEFAULT_BRANCH plus refs/heads/dev, refs/heads/staging, refs/heads/main), so the list is the union of the two rather than a per-branch selection.
`skip_job_declarations` is EMPTY because `.github/workflows/ci.yml` passes `skip_jobs: ''` — this repository skips nothing. An entry is only ever needed for a token this repository really writes.

`enforcement` is deliberately ABSENT, which means BLOCK. The seeds Lisa ships set it to `warn` so a fresh install does not go red on arrival; this snapshot has been transcribed, so the ramp does not apply.

The transcription NEVER EXPIRES (#3599). Trust is presence-based: this stamp being non-empty and parseable is what makes `required_contexts` believable, and an empty or unreadable stamp is what makes the guard refuse. A ninety-day ceiling used to sit here, paired with a scheduled workflow that re-read the live ruleset and moved the date; that workflow was removed because it needed a standing `administration:read` token. Keeping the deadline without the refresh would have left an obligation nobody can discharge. Re-run the `gh api` line above and move the date whenever the ruleset changes — nothing will remind you, and that is the accepted trade.

`evidence_bearing_checks` names the checks whose GREEN is supposed to mean something reviewed the code. `.github/workflows/review-evidence.yml` runs the vacuity arm against every pull request here; before #2928 nothing invoked it at all. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-25 (#3221) over the last 40 merged pull requests, reading the `CodeRabbit` status on each PR's HEAD SHA: all 40 reported `success`, and the descriptions were `Review skipped: manual review required for this OSS repository` 29, `Review rate limited` 10, `Review completed` 1 (#3185). The earlier 25-PR reading (9 / 14 / 2) is superseded. The 29 are a STANDING CodeRabbit-side entitlement state for a public repository, not a blip and not set in this tree — `.coderabbit.yml` never disables auto-review — so clearing it is a human action in CodeRabbit's console, not a change here. That workflow is REPORT-ONLY on purpose and can still go red for one reason that is not a finding: it inspected NOTHING. Read the `vacuity_*` token before calling a red run a hollow review.

TWO DECLARATIONS, ONE QUESTION, AND THEY ARE NOT REDUNDANT (#3591). `evidence_bearing_checks` here feeds `check-skipped-required-checks.mjs`, which answers "did the required review check do any work?" and, per the owner's ruling on #3221, WAIVES the two named entitlement phrases. `gates.code-review.pull-request.evidence` in `.lisa.config.json` feeds `check-third-party-review-evidence.mjs`, which answers the next question — "and if it did not, what read the diff instead?" — and recognises no waivers at all: only a declared `proof` phrase grants credit, and a reviewer showing none must be substituted for by a posted local adversarial review. Keep the phrases consistent between them; they are read by different provers for different decisions, so neither file can be deleted in favour of the other without losing one of the two answers.
